To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the method is able to correct the matrix effect in the presence of a 3He monitor, (2) the method has a good accuracy in the estimation of the residual mass of fissile material in a drum of metallic waste, (3) the accuracy of the method is of the order of a factor 2, (4) the method can be implemented on the industrial site, (5) the method can also be used on other active interrogation neutron measurement devices

a matrix correction method has been developed and validated for an active interrogation system, based on a combination of the MCNP code and a 3He proportional counter, and the method has been successfully applied on the ACC installation.
- A matrix correction method based on a neutron monitor (3He proportional counter) was developed and tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of a method for correcting the effects of matrix in the measurement of the mass of fissile material in the drums of radioactive waste filled with metal residues compacted (coils and ends of spent fuel produced at the reprocessing plant of La Hague) by active neutron interrogation, on the coil and ends compacting workshop (ACC).
the development of an active interrogation neutron measurement technique for fissile material in spent fuel assemblies.
the development of a methodology to correct the effects of matrix in neutron interrogation systems, based on the use of a neutron monitor (He-3 proportional counter) in the interrogation field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed is suitable for correcting the matrix effect and that it is a reliable method for the measurement of the residual fissile mass in the drums of the current waste production.

the use of the proposed matrix correction method on the 0 2 station is a promising approach, with the following conclusions : - the matrix effect is well reproduced by the MCNP code ; - the matrix correction method is able to correct the matrix effect in the case of the current production of fuel baskets with metallic scrap, and to reduce the error on the mass estimation from a few decades to less than a factor two ; - the matrix effect correction method could be applied to other interrogation devices.
the proposed approach is promising for the correction of the effects of matrix on the active interrogation neutron measurement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a method of correcting the matrix effect has been developed for the active neutron interrogation system of the ACC.
the coupling of a matrix correction method with a neutron activation interrogation system has proved to be a promising solution for the determination of fissile mass in the presence of a moderator.
the MCNP code is able to simulate the experimental results of the PROMETHEE R&D mock-up with a good accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the method of matrix effect correction based on the associated measurement of a can monitor (3He proportional counter) is a promising approach for improving the accuracy of the active interrogation neutron measurements.
the proposed method can be applied to other active interrogation systems, and that it is a valuable addition to the toolbox of nuclear safeguards.
the use of a neutron monitor in a fissile mass measurement by active interrogation is a promising method for the correction of the matrix effects.
